identifying_description: Large drum reserved for use at samb-zi, a great festive song. At the base, a curvilinear relief carving references the organic form of a wasp hive, and at the top a star or flying fox. Patterns are enhanced with white, black, and red pigments. The mammal skin is probably tree kangaroo, Dendrolagus, and the gum is blood and lime.

Drum, kandara
West Papua (Irian Jaya), South Coast, Merauke area, Marind-anim people
19th century
Wood, pigment, fiber, skin, and gum
Gift of Marcia and John Friede in honor of Diane B. Wilsey and Harry S. Parker III
2007.44.89 (cat. no. 508)

For the Marind-anim people who live on the southern coast of New Guinea, performances are an integral part of life. This large drum is reserved for samb-zi, a great festive song restricted to male participation. Drummers assemble around a big fire, heating and tightening the head of their drums, and dancers with reed and feather headdresses quietly huddle. When the drumming starts, the dancers begin moving to its moderate tempo, swinging all the ornaments hanging from their bodies. As the drummers increase their cadence, the dancers increase their speed, and their wooden phalluses swing up and down.

An elegant hourglass shape and skillfully proportioned handle distinguish this tall Marind-anim drum (kandara). Mammal skin is stretched over the top of the wooden chamber and attached using a mixture of blood and lime. Curvilinear relief carvings imitate the form of a wasp hive at the base with a star or flying fox at the top. These patterns are beautifully enhanced with white, black, and red pigments.
